driver: The priced unit is a buyer-side position that persists across the supplier's substitutions of the physical asset, so supplier-keyed asset stays must be chained into that unit through a buyer-side mapping before a length-tiered tariff re-rates each unit from its first day, and a settled history billed at a flat rate cannot show the difference.
driver_concrete: Under KLR-C7 clause 6.1 a Keystone exchange continues the same Rental, so 258 unit stays chain through the DC access-module register into 150 hires; 113 pass 56 days and bill every day at the extended rate (7.3), exchange movements are uncharged (7.4), giving $275,060.85 against $393,689.72 when each stay is priced alone.
stump: A competent solver applies the noon off-rent clock and the certificate rule correctly but prices each Keystone unit's stay as its own hire, filing $393,690 (+43.1 per cent), because every dealer record keys on fleet number and the prior peaks' invoices recompute exactly whether exchanges are chained or not.
